# indicators — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 5 · S4 E1 A4 H5 P3 · limited by hardening (no sweep, no fuzz/ct recorded) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** mvp — TA-Lib C 0.8.3, all 237 of its functions: the seed set (17), the Overlap Studies wave (27: every moving-average type, the bands / channels, SAR family, Supertrend, Ichimoku, Zig-Zag), the volume / volatility / price-transform / statistic / math-operator wave (50), the cycle wave (25: HT family, MAMA, three SWAK rows, 15 math transforms), the momentum wave (57: ADX family, AROON, ROC family, oscillators, KST / KDJ / STOCHRSI / CRSI / STC / SQZMOM, ...) and the 61 candlestick patterns (`candles.zig`). Remaining deviations from TA-Lib: MAVP has no streaming type; LINEARREG_ANGLE, PSO and the math transforms (ACOS ... TANH) carry a 2-ULP bound (libm `atan` / `tanh` rounding); the Hilbert family and MAMA a column-relative 1e-13 bound (`atan`); RSI answers NaN where TA-Lib's NaN-poisoned state reads 50; batch and streaming MAX / MIN differ in the sign of a 0.0 / -0.0 tie, as TA-Lib's two tiers do (surveyed 2026-11-15 against `ta_func.h` and the function sources of the 0.8.3 tarball)

**Audit:** review none · mutation none · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz none · ct n/a — no secret enters an indicator · panic none

**Performance:** not measured

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

## What this module is, and what it is not

Technical-analysis indicators over caller slices, numerically faithful to TA-Lib C 0.8.3: same
formulas, same order of floating-point operations, same constants, same parameter ranges and
lookbacks. Seed set: SMA, EMA, WMA, MA, MACD, MACDEXT, MACDFIX, RSI, BBANDS, TRANGE, ATR, NATR,
STOCH, STOCHF, MAX, MIN, SUM; wave I3, overlap studies: DEMA, TEMA, T3, TRIMA, KAMA, MIDPOINT, MIDPRICE, SAR, SAREXT, MAVP,
ACCBANDS, ALMA, CKSP, DONCHIAN, FRAMA, HMA, ICHIMOKU, KC, MCGD, RMA, SUPERTREND, SWAK_BUTTER, SWAK_GAUSS,
VIDYA, VWMA, ZIGZAG, ZLEMA; wave I3, volume / volatility / price transform / statistic / math operator: AD, ADOSC, CMF,
EFI, EMV, KVO, MARKETFI, NVI, OBV, PVI, PVO, PVT, RVOL, VWAP, ADR, BBW, CVI, MASSI, PERCENTB, ROGERSSATCHELL, RVI, RVIR,
AVGDEV, AVGPRICE, HA, MEDPRICE, TYPPRICE, WCLPRICE, BETA, CORREL, KURTOSIS, LINEARREG (+ANGLE / INTERCEPT / SLOPE), MEDIAN,
PERCENTILE, PERCENTRANK, STDDEV, TSF, VAR, ADD, SUB, MULT, DIV, CUMSUM, MINMAX, MAXINDEX, MININDEX, MINMAXINDEX; wave I3, cycle: HT_DCPERIOD, HT_DCPHASE, HT_PHASOR, HT_SINE, HT_TRENDLINE, HT_TRENDMODE, MAMA, SWAK_BP, SWAK_HP, SWAK_2PHP, ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, CEIL, COS, COSH, EXP, FLOOR, LN, LOG10, SIN, SINH, SQRT, TAN, TANH. Every function has a batch form, a `Lookback` function and a
streaming type (MAVP excepted, see Limits; MACDEXT, STOCH, STOCHF, CKSP and ALMA additionally take an allocator first, used only for `f32` input or scratch, see Limits); the batch and streaming forms run the same core step, so they agree to the bit
(tested).

What a reader might expect and will not find: a streaming MAVP, TA-Lib's `startIdx`/`endIdx` range arguments (a batch call covers the whole slice;
`out[0..lookback]` is NaN), in-place calls (`out` must not alias `in`; TA-Lib allows it, see Backlog), and an abstract/function-table
interface.

## Wire format / algorithm

API (settled in `indicators-I2-design.md`): `fn <name>(comptime T: type, in, out…, params) Error!usize`
with `T` in {f32, f64} (the math is f64), `out.len == in.len` for every slice (else
`error.BadParam`), the first `lookback` slots NaN, the lookback returned. OHLC functions take
`high, low, close` slices of one length. `<name>Lookback(params) Error!usize`.

Cores (`src/core.zig`, `smooth.zig`): every indicator is a by-value `step(src, x) ?f64` core
counting the bars fed to it. A core that needs older values reads them through `src.at(i)`: a view
of the caller slice (batch) or a ring buffer (streaming). A composite feeds each component from the
bar where the component's own lookback ends exactly on the bar where the composite's does
(`skip = largest lookback - own lookback`, the way TA-Lib calls `TA_MA(startIdx = lookbackLargest …)`),
which fixes the seeding window of every SMA, WMA and EMA inside it.

Per-function notes from the C source (each read before it was ported):

- **EMA**: seed = SMA of the first `period` bars (MetaStock compatibility no longer exists in 0.8.x);
  `beta = (p-1)/(p+1)`, `k = 1-beta`, `beta` re-derived as `1-k` when `beta < 0.5`;
  `prev = fma(beta, prev, k*x)` (`@mulAdd`); period 1 is a copy (keeps -0.0). Lookback
  `p - 1 + unstable`; the stored unstable count applies even at period 1 (lookback = count).
  AUTO levels (period > 1): auto4 = (10p+1)/2, auto8 = (19p+1)/2.
- **SMA/SUM**: running sum, the bar leaves after the output is read (`out = sum / p`, then `sum -= oldest`).
- **WMA**: running weighted sum and plain sum, both rebuilt from the window (oldest first, weights
  1..p) every 8p outputs (the 0.8.x re-anchor); divider `p(p+1)/2` in double.
- **MA**: period 1 and `.disabled` are a copy with lookback 0 for every type; the SMA/EMA/WMA arms
  forward; every other type is built in wave I3 and the cycle wave (see below). Period range 1..100000, default 30.
- **MACD**: fast and slow are swapped when slow < fast; slow EMA from bar 0, fast from
  `Ls - Lf`, signal from the first line bar; first output at `Ls + Lg`. Signal period 1 copies the
  line, except that TA-Lib's very first signal value is `0.0 + line` (the SMA seed of one value); kept.
- **MACDEXT**: swaps periods and types; period range of fast/slow 2.., signal 1..; every component is
  an `ma` (any supported type); line values before the signal's first bar are not reported.
- **MACDFIX**: 12/26 with the fixed pair k = 0.15 / 0.075 (not 2/(p+1)), beta = 1-k, k = 1-beta, no
  `beta < 0.5` swap; the fast EMA runs as many unstable bars as the slow one.
- **RSI**: Wilder; one delta of lead, `p` deltas summed and divided for the seed; `100*g/(g+l)`, a
  window with neither gain nor loss answers 50 (0.8.x #480). Unstable lookback `p + u`, AUTO 10p / 19p.
- **TRANGE**: lookback 1 (bar 0 only supplies the previous close). **ATR**: seed = mean of the first
  `p` true ranges, then `fma(beta, atr, alpha*tr)` with `beta = (p-1)/p`, `alpha = 1-beta`; lookback
  `p + u`, AUTO `(10(2p-1)+1)/2` and `(19(2p-1)+1)/2`. **NATR**: the same recursion, AUTO 10p / 19p,
  output `atr / close * 100` of the bar's own close (a zero close answers 0), period 1 is the raw true range.
- **BBANDS**: the deviation is the population standard deviation of the window (TA_VAR with the
  shifted running sums and the re-anchor rules ported from `ta_VAR.c`), the middle band is any
  supported MA; period 2.., dev in [-3e37, 3e37]; `upper = mid + sd*up`, `lower = mid - sd*dn` (`fma` form
  when the two deviations differ). Lookback `max(MA lookback, p-1)`.
- **STOCH/STOCHF**: raw %K = 100*(C-LL)/(HH-LL), a window flat to within 1e-14 of its magnitude answers 0;
  %D/slow lines are MAs cascading on the previous stage; the first stage reports from the last stage's first bar.
- **MAX/MIN**: window extreme with index tracking and rescan on expiry (periods 2..); **SUM** period 2..

Wave I3, overlap studies (each C function read before it was ported; same `step` cores, plus `src/hist.zig` for the
multi-input functions: a core reads the bar history through `h.at(i)` of a struct of f64 fields, outputs are
one slice per field):

- **DEMA / TEMA / T3** (`mavg.zig`, one `ChainCore`): K EMAs in lockstep, each seeded with the mean of its first `p`
  inputs. DEMA/TEMA start stage `j` at bar `j * L_ema` (every stage skips the unstable bars), lookback
  `K * L_ema`, EMA's beta/k pair; period 1 copies after `K * unstable` bars (the C comment: TA_MA reports 0, the
  function itself `K * unstable`, they disagree when the unstable period is non-zero; kept). T3 starts stage `j`
  at `j (p-1)` and adds the unstable bars at the end (lookback `6(p-1) + u`, AUTO `(11*8p+7)/8` / `(11*12p+7)/8`),
  uses `k = 2/(p+1)` and `1-k` without the beta swap, and the coefficients `c1..c4` of vfactor in `fma` form
  (`vfactor` in [0,1], default 0.7).
- **TRIMA**: the 0.8.x four-adjustment running numerator (odd and even period differ in the middle weight),
  period 1 is not a copy (`0.0 + x` seeds, so -0.0 becomes +0.0), as TA-Lib.
- **KAMA**: efficiency ratio from a running sum of absolute one-bar changes, clamped to 1; a window whose every
  change is exactly zero (run counter `nullRun`) resets the sum (0.8.x); the smoothing constant is
  `(er*(2/3-2/31) + 2/31)^2` with `fma`; lookback `p + u` (AUTO `100 root`, `200 root`, `root = floor(sqrt p)`); period 1 copies after `u` bars.
- **ZLEMA**: EMA of `2 x[t] - x[t-lag]`, `lag = (p-1)/2`, lookback `lag + p-1 + u`.
- **RMA**: Wilder, seed = mean of `p`, `fma(beta, prev, alpha*x)` with `beta = (p-1)/p`, `alpha = 1-beta`;
  lookback `p-1+u`, AUTO `(10(2p-1)+1)/2`, `(19(2p-1)+1)/2`; period 1 is not special-cased.
- **VIDYA**: EMA with `k = alpha * |CMO|`, CMO over `cmo_period` (2..) changes (the CMOU loop incl. the exact-flat
  reset); lookback `cmo + u`; as an `MaType` the CMO period is `(3p+2)/4`.
- **HMA**: `WMA(2 WMA(x, p/2) - WMA(x, p), floor(sqrt p))`; TA-Lib's fused pass is bit-identical to the
  composition of three TA_WMA runs (their re-anchors included), so the core composes three `WmaCore`s and keeps the
  de-lagged series in a 316-slot ring inside the core (`sqrt(100000)`); lookback `p-1 + s-1`; period 1 copies.
- **ALMA**: Gaussian weights `exp(-(j-m)^2/(2 s^2))/norm`, `m = floor(offset (p-1))`, `s = p/sigma`
  (sigma >= 0.01, offset in [0,1]); the batch function builds the table once (stack up to 64, else `gpa`), the `MaType` and
  the stream recompute each weight (same bits); `exp` is `@exp` (compiler-rt) and agrees with glibc on every compared value.
- **MCGD**: `md += (x-md) / (p (x/md)^4)`, an update that would be non-finite is dropped; period 2..; lookback `p-1+u`.
- **SWAK_BUTTER / SWAK_GAUSS**: two-pole filters, period 2..10000 (not 100000), lookback = the unstable count only
  (AUTO `(13(p+2)+8)/9`, `(22(p+2)+8)/9`), state seeded with the first bar; `sin`/`sqrt` as in the C.
- **MIDPOINT / MIDPRICE / DONCHIAN**: `(highest + lowest)/2` over `p` (2..); DONCHIAN also reports both extremes.
  **ICHIMOKU**: tenkan/kijun/senkou-B midprice windows, senkou-A = `(tenkan+kijun)/2`, no displacement, lookback = longest-1.
- **ACCBANDS**: running sums of `h(1+4(h-l)/(h+l))`, `l(1-...)`, `c`; a bar whose `h+l` is within 1e-14 of its own
  magnitude adds `h`, `l` unwidened; the trailing term is recomputed from the history.
- **KC**: EMA of the typical price `(h+l+c)/3` and ATR (each fed from the bar where its own lookback ends on the
  channel's first bar), `mid +/- ATR*nb_dev`; both take the unstable option.
- **FRAMA**: period even (odd = BadParam), midpoint price, `alpha = exp(-4.6 (D-1))` from the half-window ranges, reset to the price when the
  ranges are degenerate; lookback `p + u` (AUTO `min(9*8(root+2)/2, 990)`, `min(9*12(root+2)/2, 1881)`); the exact window extremes are
  all that matters, so the C's Van Herk slot scheme is replaced by two `ExtCore` pairs (second pair on the half window that ended `p/2` bars ago).
- **VWMA**: `sum(c v)/sum(v)` as `(PV/p)/(V/p)`; a window of exactly zero volume answers NaN (0/0) and resets the sums.
- **MAVP**: per-bar period from a second series, clamped to [min, max] and truncated (NaN gives min), the average of
  that period at that bar, each period run as TA_MA runs it from the first output bar (`startIdx = lookback of max_period`),
  periods 1..10000.
- **SAR / SAREXT**: one state machine (`SarCore(ext)`); the first direction from TA_MINUS_DM with period 1; SAREXT reports the short side negative, supports
  `start_value` and `offset_on_reverse`; lookback 1; accelerations clamp to their maxima as in the C.
- **SUPERTREND**: ATR (the existing `AtrCore`, unstable option) bands around `(h+l)/2` that only tighten while the trend holds; `trend` is `i8` (1 or -1; 0 in the lead);
  period 2.., multiplier [0, 3e37]. **CKSP**: first stops `highest high(p) - m ATR` / `lowest low(p) + m ATR`, then the max / min of the last
  `stop_period` first stops (scratch ring `2 q`); lookback `ATR lookback + q-1`, plus `q-1` more with an AUTO unstable level.
  **ZIGZAG**: percent reversal from bar 0's low, outputs `zigzag` (pivot), `trend` (`i8`), `pivot_idx` (`i32`); lookback = `min_trend_length`.
- **MA with the new types**: every type of `MaType` (MAMA came with the cycle wave) works in MA / MACDEXT / BBANDS / STOCH / STOCHF (period 1 and DISABLED still copy);
  fixed side parameters as TA_MA: T3 vfactor 0.7, VIDYA CMO period `(3p+2)/4`, ALMA sigma 6 offset 0.85. **BBANDS** starts the average at bar 0 and the deviation late
  (TA_BBANDS calls TA_MA with startIdx 0 and realigns): this differs from "feed from the largest lookback" exactly when the average's lookback is
  below the deviation's (VIDYA, found by the oracle; DISABLED copies, so it never showed).
### Volume, volatility, price-transform, statistic and math-operator functions (wave I3)

50 more functions, each read from its `ta_<NAME>.c` before it was ported, each with a batch form, a
`<name>Lookback` and a streaming type, all verified bitwise against TA-Lib 0.8.3 (see Anchoring):

- **Volume** (`src/volume.zig`): AD, ADOSC, CMF, EFI, EMV, KVO, MARKETFI, NVI, OBV, PVI, PVO, PVT, RVOL, VWAP.
- **Volatility** (`src/volatility.zig`): ADR, BBW, CVI, MASSI, PERCENTB, ROGERSSATCHELL, RVI, RVIR.
- **Price transform** (`src/pricetx.zig`): AVGDEV, AVGPRICE, HA, MEDPRICE, TYPPRICE, WCLPRICE.
- **Statistic** (`src/statistic.zig`): BETA, CORREL, KURTOSIS, LINEARREG, LINEARREG_ANGLE, LINEARREG_INTERCEPT,
  LINEARREG_SLOPE, MEDIAN, PERCENTILE, PERCENTRANK, STDDEV, TSF, VAR (named `variance`: `var` is a keyword).
- **Math operators** (`src/mathops.zig`): ADD, SUB, MULT, DIV, CUMSUM, MINMAX, MAXINDEX, MININDEX, MINMAXINDEX.

API additions (same rules as the seed set, see the design doc): OHLCV inputs are separate slices in the order of the
TA-Lib prototype (`ad(T, high, low, close, volume, out)`), several outputs are one slice each (`kvo`, `ha`, `minmax`),
the multi-input streaming types take a struct (`update(.{ .high = h, .low = l, .close = c, .volume = v })`; the
single-series ones keep `update(x)`), functions without parameters have a `<name>Lookback()` without arguments and no
`p`. Every function is a tuple core of `src/vs_kit.zig`: a by-value `step(src, in)` that reads older bars through
`src.at(i)` (the caller's slices in batch, a ring of tuples in a caller buffer when streaming), so batch and
streaming agree to the bit (tested for every function, `peek` included). Where the C keeps a ring of *derived* values
(CVI's EMA, MASSI's ratio, EMV's and CMF's one-bar terms, ROGERSSATCHELL's terms) the value that leaves the window is
recomputed from the input ring (CVI and MASSI run a second copy of the recursion `lag` bars behind): the same
operations on the same inputs give the identical double, and nothing needs a scratch array. MEDIAN and PERCENTILE keep
a sorted copy of the window and therefore take `gpa` (batch) or a larger caller buffer (stream, `bufLen`).

Notes from the C sources:

- **ADOSC**: both EMAs seed on the first A/D value; fast and slow are NOT swapped (ADOSC(10,3) = EMA10 - EMA3);
  lookback `EMA_Lookback(slowest) +` the Auto offset `(15m + 3*sum_{k=1..16} min(M>>k, m) + 7)/8` (m, M = min/max period),
  AUTO only. **KVO**: the 1997 factor `|2*(dm/cm) - 1|`, trend ties keep the previous trend, `cm` restarts on a trend change,
  the three EMAs seed raw on the first volume force; lookback `1 + EMA_Lookback(longest)` + the Auto offset
  `(21L+1)/2 - (10L+1)/2` (auto4) or `(33L+1)/2 - (19L+1)/2` (auto8). **EFI**: EMA (SMA seed) of `(close - previous close) * volume`.
- **CMF / RVOL**: a window of zero volumes resets the sums to exactly 0 (the C's dead-window rule, #112). RVOL's baseline
  excludes today (lookback = period). **EMV**: SMA of `(mid - previous mid) / (volume/divisor/range)`, 0 where range or the
  box ratio is 0; divisor 1..3e37. **MARKETFI** `(high-low)/volume`, 0 for zero volume. **VWAP** is cumulative from the first
  bar (the anchor is the caller's slice); a bar with a non-finite price or volume is skipped; 0 before any volume.
  **NVI / PVI** are seeded at 1000, move only when the volume fell / rose and the previous close is not 0, and keep the last finite value.
  **PVT**, **OBV**, **AD** as in the C. **PVO**: `(fast MA - slow MA) / slow MA * 100` of the volume, MA type default EMA, fast/slow
  swapped when slow < fast; a slow MA within 1e-14 of 0 answers 0, and for the windowed MA types (SMA, WMA, TRIMA, HMA) so does a
  window of `period` zero volumes.
- **BBW / PERCENTB** are BBANDS' bands (same plan: MA of any supported type started at bar 0 and the deviation late, as BBANDS, population deviation, `fma` form when the two
  multipliers differ); BBW = `(upper - lower)/middle*100` (0 for a zero middle), %B = `(x - lower)/(upper - lower)` (0.5 for a zero-width band).
- **CVI**: `100 * ((E - E[-roc]) / E[-roc])` over the EMA of `high - low`, 0 for a lagged EMA of exactly 0; lookback `EMA_Lookback(p) + roc`.
  **MASSI**: two stacked EMAs of `high - low` (the second starts at the callee's EMA lookback, which includes the unstable bars, so the
  lookback shifts by 2u), ratio 1 for a zero second EMA, summed over `slow` bars. **ADR** = SMA of `high - low`.
  **ROGERSSATCHELL**: `sqrt(A) * sqrt(mean of ln(H/C)ln(H/O) + ln(L/C)ln(L/O))`, a bar with a price <= 0 contributes 0, the running sum is
  rebuilt below 1e-6 of its peak and every 32 windows; `sqrt(A)` stays a separate last factor. **RVI**: the variance step of `ta_VAR.c`
  (anchored at bar 0), sigma credited to the up or down side by the close change, each side Wilder-smoothed with a mean seed, 50 when both are 0; lookback
  `stddev - 1 + period - 1 + u` with `u` = bars, 10p (auto4), 19p (auto8; 0 at period 1). **RVIR** = `0.5 * (RVI(high) + RVI(low))`.
- **AVGDEV** recomputes the window every bar (O(n*period), newest bar first, as the C). **HA**: haOpen `(O+C)/2` then `(haOpen+haClose)/2`,
  haClose `(O+H+L+C)/4` (open first, unlike AVGPRICE's `((H+L)+C)+O`), haHigh/haLow by plain comparisons; lookback = unstable bars, AUTO 15 / 28.
  **WCLPRICE** fuses the doubled close into the sum (`fma`).
- **VAR** validates but ignores `nbdev` (as TA_VAR); **STDDEV** `sqrt(var) * nbdev` (`sqrt(var)` at exactly 1). **LINEARREG / SLOPE / ANGLE / INTERCEPT / TSF**
  are one core: sums slid in O(1), rebuilt every 32 periods and when the departing value outweighs 100x the window's magnitude; `value = fma(m, p-1, b)`,
  `forecast = fma(m, p, b)`, `angle = atan(m) * (180/pi)`. **CORREL / BETA / KURTOSIS** keep the C's shifted sums, re-anchor triggers
  (1e-6 of the peak; BETA also when an outlier return leaves: 1000x), floors and clamps; KURTOSIS is G2 (period 4..10000), NaN for a flat window.
  **MEDIAN / PERCENTILE / PERCENTRANK**: periods 2..10000; the median of an even window is the mean of the two central values; PERCENTILE is the nearest rank
  `ceil(P*n/100)` clamped to 1..n; PERCENTRANK counts the previous `period` bars strictly below today (lookback = period).
- **MINMAX / MAXINDEX / MININDEX / MINMAXINDEX**: periods 2..; the indices are absolute positions in the input slice (`outInteger`), a tie names the newest bar,
  the lead of an index output is `no_index` (`maxInt(usize)`). **ADD / SUB / MULT / DIV / CUMSUM** are plain IEEE (division by zero gives inf / NaN as in C).

Where this port differs from the C, and why:

- LINEARREG_ANGLE calls libm's `atan`; TA-Lib uses the C library's, we use `std.math.atan`. Both are within an ULP of the exact value but round
  differently, and the 180/pi scaling can stretch that to 2 ULP of the result (14 of 15066 compared values; the oracle's `ulp_bound` for this one
  function is 2). Every other function, ROGERSSATCHELL's `log` and every `sqrt` included, is bitwise equal.
- MEDIAN / PERCENTILE: TA-Lib picks linear or binary search by window size and has a 700-line optimised PERCENTILE kernel; we use one binary
  search and the plain definition (equal values stay in age order, so zeros keep their sign, as the C documents). On finite data these agree bit for bit
  (oracle); with NaN inputs the order inside the sorted copy is unspecified in both.
- MAX / MIN / MINMAX: TA-Lib's batch uses a block (van Herk / Gil-Werman) scan and its streaming tier a per-bar automaton, and they disagree on the sign of a tie between
  0.0 and -0.0 (measured with the oracle's tie inputs, kind 3). The batch functions reproduce the block scan (`window.extBatch`, scratch-free); the streaming types
  run the automaton, as TA-Lib's streaming tier does, so for such ties a batch call and a stream differ in the sign of the zero (and in where a NaN shows), as TA-Lib's two tiers do.
  MAXINDEX & co tie to the newest bar like the C (oracle-checked on the same inputs).
- Per-call unstable period instead of a process-global one (as the seed set); `nan = .skip` is not offered on these functions.
- The Auto levels (`unstable = .auto4 / .auto8`) are checked for ADOSC, EFI, KVO, CVI, MASSI, PVO, RVI, RVIR, HA, BBW and PERCENTB.

### Cycle wave: Hilbert-transform family, MAMA, Swiss Army Knife rows, math transforms
- **HT_DCPERIOD / HT_DCPHASE / HT_PHASOR / HT_SINE / HT_TRENDLINE / HT_TRENDMODE / MAMA** (`cycle.zig`, one `Hil` core): the 4-bar weighted price smoother (initialised
  like TA_WMA with three bars unrolled), the even / odd detrender and quadrature stages with their 3-slot delays (`hilbertIdx` advances on even bars only, as in
  the C), `adjustedPrevPeriod = fma(0.075, period, 0.54)`, the `Re`/`Im` smoothing and the clamped period estimate, constants as typed f64 and every `fma` of the C as `@mulAdd`.
  TA-Lib starts all seven at the first input and only withholds the output, so the recursion is anchored at bar 0 and the even / odd split follows the
  ABSOLUTE bar index (`today % 2`): batch and stream agree to the bit, and the lookback is a fixed count plus the unstable period (32 for DCPERIOD, PHASOR, MAMA; 63 for the
  others; AUTO levels `80 + 50*4` / `80 + 50*8` (+ `ceil(20 / max(fast, slow))` / `ceil(38 / max)` for MAMA), `120 + 20*4` / `120 + 20*8` for TRENDLINE and TRENDMODE).
  The transform itself starts at bar 12 (DCPERIOD, PHASOR, MAMA) or 37 (the rest: the C's smoother loop is 9 or 34 bars long). DCPHASE, SINE and TRENDMODE sum the
  last `(int)(smoothPeriod + 0.5)` smoothed prices (a 50-slot ring) with `sin` / `cos`; TRENDLINE and TRENDMODE average the RAW price over the same count (issue #88 of TA-Lib:
  not the smoothed price); `(int)` of a NaN is 0 as the C guards it. PHASOR reports the in-phase component of the bar's own parity (`I1ForEven/OddPrev3`) and `Q1`.
  MAMA: alpha from the phase of `Q1 / I1`, `mama = fma(1 - a, mama, a x)`, `fama` from `a / 2`; limits [0.01, 0.99], fast default 0.5, slow 0.05.
  Unstable option and `nan` on all of them; no history buffer (the core keeps its two 50-slot rings, copy by value).
- **MaType.mama** (TA_MA): period ignored (limits 0.5 / 0.05), the MAMA line is the output, lookback 32 + unstable (AUTO `80 + 50*4 + 40` / `80 + 50*8 + 76`); a period of 1 still copies. It works in
  every slot that takes a `MaType` (MACDEXT, BBANDS, STOCH, STOCHF, MAVP, PVO, BBW, PERCENTB) and in the oracle's grids for them. `error.Unsupported` is no longer returned (kept in the error set).
- **SWAK_BP / SWAK_HP / SWAK_2PHP**: Ehlers' band-pass (period 5..2000, delta 0.05..0.5), one-pole high-pass (period 5..100000) and two-pole high-pass (period 2..10000) rows; the state starts in the
  steady state of a constant input equal to the first bar (a DC-gain-zero row answers 0 there, tested), lookback = the unstable count only (BP AUTO `ceil(11 p / 6 delta)` / `ceil(20 p / 6 delta)`,
  HP `(10p+5)/6` / `(19p+5)/6`, 2PHP as BUTTER), `a1*y1` is the outermost `fma` as the C comments insist. Bitwise equal to TA-Lib.
- **Math transforms** (`mathtx.zig`): element-wise, lookback 0, no parameters, `T` in {f32, f64}; a value outside the domain is NaN or an infinity, as in C. CEIL, FLOOR, SQRT are exact; EXP, LN, LOG10, SIN, COS, TAN
  are Zig's builtins (compiler-rt) and agree with the oracle's glibc on all 31883 compared values each; ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, SINH, COSH, TANH are `xmath.zig`'s (see below).
- **`xmath.zig`**: Zig has no builtin for the inverse trigonometric and the hyperbolic functions and `std.math`'s `atan` differs from glibc's in the last bit in 0.3% of the results, and the plain fdlibm form `0.5 * exp(x)` of `sinh` / `cosh` at |x| ~ 100 in 5%.
  ACOS / ASIN / ATAN are evaluated in double-double (half-angle reduction, Taylor series, one final rounding: correctly rounded but for a ~1e-30 sliver); SINH / COSH / TANH follow fdlibm's formulas
  with a double-double exponential from |x| = 22 up. Against glibc: ACOS 2, ASIN 11, ATAN 8, COSH 368, SINH 50 and TANH 3 of 31883 values differ (by 1 ULP, SINH and TANH in a few places by 2), so the six carry an allowance
  of 2 ULP (`ulp_bound`); glibc is not correctly rounded and no portable reproduction of its rounding exists short of porting its (LGPL) tables.
- **Reference allowance for the recursive Hilbert family.** HT_DCPERIOD / HT_DCPHASE / HT_PHASOR / HT_SINE and MAMA feed `atan(Im / Re)` back into the filter. Where glibc's `atan` and ours round differently
  (ATAN alone: 8 of 31883 arguments), the two runs differ in a last bit that the recursion carries along: measured over the whole grid the largest difference is 1.0e-15 of the output's own maximum
  (HT_SINE; MAMA 2.8e-16; in ULPs up to 1085 on HT_PHASOR, where an output crosses zero). The oracle therefore allows `1e-13` of the column maximum (`scaled_bound`) for these five, `1e-12` for any other
  function whose MA slot is MAMA (PERCENTB, measured 3.9e-15, divides by the band width), and 0 for everything else. The same run with `std.math.atan` instead gave up to 19425 ULP on MACDEXT with MAMA (and four to ten times more mismatching records):
  the correctly rounded `atan` is what makes the allowance this small. HT_TRENDLINE and HT_TRENDMODE (their outputs depend on the integer cycle length and on a 1.5% threshold) and the SWAK rows are bitwise equal. TA-Lib itself,
  built without `-ffp-contract=off`, contracts `a*b + c` inside its `fma` target clone and answers differently per CPU: the oracle archive is built with the official flags.

### Candlestick patterns (61 functions, `candles.zig`)

All 61 `CDL*` functions of TA-Lib 0.8.3 (Pattern Recognition), ported from each `ta_CDL*.c`; reached as `ind.candles.<name>` (`cdl2crows`, `cdldoji`, ... with `<name>Lookback`, `<Name>Stream`, `<Name>Params`),
`ind.candles.names` lists them.

- **Output** `[]i32` like TA-Lib's `outInteger`: 0 no pattern, `+-100` bullish / bearish, `+-80` for the weaker ENGULFING / HARAMI / HARAMICROSS form (the second body only touches the first), `+-200` for a confirmed HIKKAKE / HIKKAKEMOD;
  the first `lookback` slots are 0 (TA-Lib has no lead, `outBegIdx` says where the output starts; the batch returns that index). Streaming `update` returns `?i32`, null until the lookback is met.
- **Settings.** TA-Lib's candle settings (BodyLong, BodyVeryLong, BodyShort, BodyDoji, ShadowLong, ShadowVeryLong, ShadowShort, ShadowVeryShort, Near, Far, Equal: range type real body / high-low / shadows, averaging period, factor)
  are process-global there (`TA_SetCandleSettings`). Ours is `CandleSettings` (`.default` = TA-Lib's table) in every call's params; the lookback and the period totals follow it. Ranges: `avg_period` 0 .. 100000 (TA-Lib: 0 .. `TA_INDEX_MAX`;
  a larger value is `error.BadParam`), `factor` finite and >= 0 (TA-Lib's own check). The seven penetration patterns (ABANDONEDBABY, DARKCLOUDCOVER, EVENINGDOJISTAR, EVENINGSTAR, MATHOLD, MORNINGDOJISTAR, MORNINGSTAR) take
  `.penetration` (0 .. 3e37; defaults 0.3 / 0.5 as in the table).
- **Machinery, built once** (`candles_core.zig`): TA_CANDLERANGE / TA_CANDLEAVERAGE, and per pattern a declared list of period totals (setting, bar offset): initialised in ascending bar order at the lookback and updated after each bar as
  `total += range(i-b) - range(i-b-period)`, the C's order, so every threshold is the C's bit for bit. One `Engine` runs the batch (a view of the caller's slices) and the stream (a ring of the last `lookback + 1` bars in a caller buffer:
  `bufLen`, `init`, `update`, `peek`, `value`, `clone`), so batch == stream. The pattern bodies (`candles_a.zig`, `candles_b.zig`) are the C conditions, transcribed in the C's order.
- **TA-Lib quirks reproduced.** Lookbacks larger than the bars used (CDL3OUTSIDE 3, CDLENGULFING 2, CDLXSIDEGAP3METHODS 2: `outBegIdx` is that, the extra bars are skipped). HIKKAKE and HIKKAKEMOD run the C's pre-warm: the three bars before the first
  output are judged (and discarded) to start the confirmation state, HIKKAKEMOD's Near total runs from there too (`warm_bars`); HIKKAKEMOD's lookback is `max(1, near period) + 5`. CDLTRISTAR measures all three bodies against the Doji average of bar `i-2`.
  `fma` is used exactly where the C writes it (ABANDONEDBABY third-bar white branch, MORNINGSTAR / MORNINGDOJISTAR, PIERCING and THRUSTING with 0.5), plain `a - b*c` where it does not (the archive is built with `-ffp-contract=off`).
  CDLGAPSIDESIDEWHITE's sign follows the first gap; KICKINGBYLENGTH signs by the longer body, KICKING by the second bar.
- **Evidence** (live oracle, see `tools/README.md`): all 61 bitwise equal (the integer outputs compared exactly), f64 and `TA_S_*`, every default and four settings presets (`TA_SetCandleSettings`: moved range types, periods, factors, period 0,
  long periods), every penetration value incl. out-of-range, lengths 1, 2, lookback-1 .. lookback+2, 40, 300, 3000, and a pattern-rich generator (single-bar shapes and multi-bar motifs, a 0.25 price grid for exact ties, a 1e-9 scale) that
  makes every pattern fire: the oracle reports, per function, how many compared values were nonzero (all 61 >= 20, smallest in the report).

## Limits and refusals

- Periods 1..100000 (2.. where TA-Lib requires it: MAX, MIN, SUM, RSI, MACD fast and slow, BBANDS);
  `Unstable.bars <= 2^30`; BBANDS deviations within ±3e37 (TA-Lib's `TA_REAL_MAX`). Pinned by the
  `BadParam` tests of each file.
- Wave I3 ranges are TA-Lib's: DEMA/TEMA/TRIMA/KAMA/ZLEMA/RMA/HMA/VWMA/VIDYA period 1.., MIDPOINT/MIDPRICE/MCGD/DONCHIAN/ACCBANDS/KC/ICHIMOKU/CKSP/SUPERTREND 2.., SWAK 2..10000,
  MAVP 1..10000 with `min <= max`, T3 vfactor [0,1], ALMA sigma [0.01, 3e37] offset [0,1], SAR/SAREXT parameters [0, 3e37] (start value ±3e37), ZIGZAG sensitivity [0,100], FRAMA even.
- No streaming type for MAVP (a per-bar period needs one average per period: a bank of up to 10000 cores). Streams of CKSP take their scratch in the caller buffer;
  `clone` of a stream re-binds it. CKSP and ALMA batch take an allocator first (CKSP: `2 * stop_period` f64 scratch, ALMA: the weight table above 64 weights).
- `nan = .skip` exists on the recursive functions that never read history (DEMA, TEMA, T3, RMA, MCGD, SWAK, SUPERTREND, KC); not on KAMA / ZLEMA / VIDYA (they read a window, as SMA).
- Integer outputs (SUPERTREND `trend`, ZIGZAG `trend` and `pivot_idx`, HT_TRENDMODE `trend`) are integer slices, 0 in the lead.
- Cycle wave ranges are TA-Lib's: the Hilbert family takes none, MAMA limits [0.01, 0.99] (NaN refused), SWAK_BP period 5..2000 and delta [0.05, 0.5], SWAK_HP 5..100000, SWAK_2PHP 2..10000. `nan = .skip` exists on all of them but the math transforms.
- No allocation on the batch path except MACDEXT, STOCH and STOCHF with `f32` input; streaming types that keep a window take a caller buffer and refuse
  a short one with `error.BadParam`. MACDEXT, STOCH and STOCHF keep their intermediate series (MACD line, raw %K, slow %K) in f64: with `f64` the output slices double as that scratch and nothing is allocated; with `f32` they allocate `n` (MACDEXT, STOCHF) or `2n` (STOCH) f64 from the `gpa` argument and free it before returning (`error.OutOfMemory`).
- Deliberate differences from TA-Lib: per-call unstable period instead of a process-global one;
  RSI answers NaN (not 50) when its internal state is NaN: TA-Lib tests `gain + loss > 0` and a NaN
  fails that test, so a poisoned RSI would read as the neutral 50, which looks like a valid
  reading, while NaN says "no value" (batch and stream agree). `nan = .skip` exists only here: a NaN
  bar leaves the state untouched and the OUTPUT at that bar carries the previous output (NaN while
  there is none), like pandas `ewm(ignore_na=True)`; the bar does not count towards the lookback.
  For `f32` input all intermediate series are f64 (as in TA-Lib's `TA_S_*`) and the result is
  rounded once on writing `out` (tested: f32 output == `@floatCast` of the f64 output for the
  f32-rounded input).

## Anchoring

**External anchor, live:** `tools/interop.zig` drives TA-Lib C 0.8.3 (our own compile of its audited
sources into a static archive, behind the C shim `tools/talib_oracle.c`; `zig build interop-indicators`)
over 9861 records: every seed and wave-I3 function (94 in all), f64 input (`TA_<F>`) and f32 input (`TA_S_<F>`), seeded
random-walk OHLC inputs (also flat-run and 1e-9-scaled kinds), a parameter grid with defaults, edges,
swapped fast/slow, every `MaType` (MAMA from the cycle wave on) in every MA slot and out-of-range values, the unstable period at
0, 3, AUTO4 and AUTO8 (`TA_SetUnstablePeriod`), and lengths 1, 2, period-1, period, period+1,
lookback..lookback+2, 40, 300 and (first parameter set) 5000; VWMA and MAVP get a second generated series (volume with zero stretches; periods -1..15 with NaN), the integer outputs travel as doubles. It compares the return code (BadParam
against `TA_BAD_PARAM`), the lookback against `TA_<F>_Lookback`, `outBegIdx == lookback` and
`outNBElement == n - lookback`, the NaN lead, and every value. **Result (2026-11-15): all 2.2 million
compared values are bitwise equal except LINEARREG_ANGLE's (ULP bound 2, see above), the per-function ULP bound is 0 for every other function incl. ALMA / FRAMA / SWAK (`exp`, `log`, `sin` from compiler-rt agree with the oracle's libm on every sampled input; not a guarantee for all inputs)** (TA-Lib 0.8.3,
x86-64, our `cc` line). One disagreement was found on the first run and it was ours: `MACDFIX` built its
0.15/0.075 pair from untyped float literals, which Zig folds at more than double precision, so
`1 - (1 - 0.15)` differed from TA-Lib's double-by-double value by up to 6e7 ULP; fixed (typed `f64`
constants), pinned by the oracle. Wave I3 brought one more, also ours (not TA-Lib's): BBANDS fed its moving average from the largest lookback, TA-Lib starts it at bar 0; the two agree unless the average's lookback is below the deviation's, which VIDYA is (see the BBANDS note); BBW and PERCENTB, which call BBANDS in TA-Lib, had inherited the same flaw and were fixed the same way when the merged oracle widened their MA grid to every type. The oracle found no defect in TA-Lib, so there is no "lead" to record.

**External anchor, frozen:** `src/testdata/talib_vectors.zig` holds 459 of those records (n = 40, the
first parameter sets of each function, one f32 record per function, AUTO4 and bars unstable) as bit
patterns of TA-Lib's answers; `src/oracle_test.zig` replays them in the ordinary test lane. Regenerate
with `zig build interop-indicators -- --emit-vectors modules/indicators/src/testdata/talib_vectors.zig`, then `zig fmt` it.

Not covered by the oracle: `nan = .skip` and `seed = .first` (options TA-Lib does not have; tested against
our own batch/stream definitions), the windowed functions with NaN input (TA-Lib's own behaviour is
unspecified; pinned by tests), parameters beyond the grid, optimised modes, other libm implementations.

**Anchor grade:** class B · oracle EXTERNAL

The volume / volatility / price-transform / statistic / math-operator functions use the same oracle with OHLCV series (volume 0..2000 with runs of zeros, zero on every flat
bar; the open inside each bar), parameter grids of defaults, edges, every `MaType` wherever a function takes one (PVO, BBW, PERCENTB), out-of-range values (every one
agrees on `TA_BAD_PARAM`), unstable 0 / 3 / AUTO4 / AUTO8 where it matters, and the lengths above; index outputs (MAXINDEX, MININDEX, MINMAXINDEX) are compared as integers.
**Result: all compared values bitwise equal except LINEARREG_ANGLE (ULP bound 2, see above); no TA-Lib defect found.**
Not covered: NaN inputs, other toolchains.

**Cycle wave (same oracle, 11867 records and 2.98 million values in all with the 94 earlier functions; every MaType including MAMA now in every MA slot):** the Hilbert family and MAMA are run
on 26 and 134 records (walk, flat-run and 1e-9-scaled inputs, lengths up to 5000, unstable 0 / 3 / AUTO4 / AUTO8 on lengths up to 700 so the AUTO warm-ups produce values, f32 via `TA_S_*`), the math transforms
get inputs inside their domains (ACOS / ASIN on [-1.2, 1.2] behind a head of edge values: 0, -0, +-1, +-(1+eps), +-inf, NaN, 710, -745, 1e22, 1e-310) and over ten decades of both signs, 16 records each, n up to 5000.
Result: SWAK_BP / HP / 2PHP, HT_TRENDLINE, HT_TRENDMODE, CEIL, FLOOR, SQRT, EXP, LN, LOG10, SIN, COS, TAN and every moving average / band / oscillator slot with MAMA (MA, MACDEXT, BBANDS, STOCH, STOCHF, MAVP, PVO, BBW) are bitwise
equal; HT_DCPERIOD (297 of 12718 values), HT_DCPHASE, HT_PHASOR, HT_SINE, MAMA and PERCENTB with MAMA differ as described under the Hilbert allowance above (largest column-relative distance 1.0e-15),
ACOS / ASIN / ATAN / COSH / SINH / TANH by at most 1 ULP (2 for SINH / TANH). `max/colmax` is printed by the oracle.

**Candlestick patterns (same oracle, 47063 records in all with the other 176 functions; the 61 patterns: 28203 records, 3.60 million compared values, all bitwise equal, no TA-Lib defect found):** every pattern at TA-Lib's default settings over lengths 1, 2, lookback-1 .. lookback+2, 40, 300 and
3000 (pattern-rich inputs, a 0.25 price grid for exact ties and a 1e-9 scale), f64 and `TA_S_*`; the seven penetration patterns at 0, 0.1, 0.3 / 0.5, 1, 3, 3e37 and the out-of-range / NaN values (BadParam on both sides); and four settings presets (every range type /
period / factor moved, all periods 0, all periods 20 with doubled factors, rotated range types with 1-2 bar periods) driven into TA-Lib with `TA_SetCandleSettings` and into ours as `CandleSettings`, which shows each setting is honoured, not only
the defaults. The oracle prints per pattern how many compared values had a nonzero TA-Lib answer: all 61 reach at least 29 (TRISTAR 29, KICKING 33, STICKSANDWICH 38, MATHOLD 46, ... CDLBELTHOLD about 16000), so no pattern is compared on zeros alone. Not covered: patterns on
inputs with NaN or infinite bars, settings with factors above 2 or periods above 20, other toolchains.

## What is deliberately not done

- Not now: `nan = .skip` on the windowed indicators; a streaming MAVP.
- Not now: SIMD fast paths, benchmark against TA-Lib and `kand` (wave I4).
- Never: process-global configuration (unstable period, candle settings) — options are per call.

## Open

- The Hilbert family and MAMA are within a column-relative 1e-13, not bitwise, because of the C library's `atan` rounding (see the cycle section); a port of glibc's `atan`
  (IBM Accurate Mathematical Library tables, LGPL) would be needed to be bitwise, and is not done. Records with `MaType.mama` inherit it.
- Bitwise agreement with TA-Lib is measured for one toolchain (x86-64, the coordinator's `cc` line); a
  TA-Lib compiled with a different contraction policy could differ by an ULP where its C spells
  `a*b - c*d` (BBANDS/VAR variance); we never contract. Re-run the oracle on aarch64 before claiming it there.
- NaN semantics of the windowed indicators (SMA, WMA, SUM, BBANDS, STOCH): a NaN enters the running
  sums and stays there until a re-anchor (WMA every 8p outputs, the variance every 32 windows)
  rebuilds them; pinned by tests, equal to TA-Lib's C by reading, not by running. MAX/MIN/MINMAX batch: the block scan of
  the C, so a NaN suffix of a block stays in the outputs that use it (pinned, by reading; the oracle has no NaN inputs);
  streams: a NaN never wins a comparison and only shows when it opens a rescan; ties keep the OLDEST value on a rescan
  (`>` / `<`) and the NEWEST on an incremental update (`>=` / `<=`) (pinned).

## Backlog / deferred

- A streaming MAVP (bank of averages, caller buffer): TA-Lib 0.8 has a streaming API for every function, MAVP included, so this is a gap against the reference, not only a design choice.
- In-place calls (`out` aliasing `in`): TA-Lib allows them, the batch functions here do not.
- Streaming for the windowed indicators with a ring that is shared between components of one composite
  (BBANDS keeps two rings of the same window for SMA).

## Momentum group (wave ind-momentum)

57 TA-Lib 0.8.3 momentum functions, each a core in the `vs_kit.zig` contract (input struct, `step(src, in)`,
batch driver, streaming type with `update` / `peek` / `value`): ADX ADXR DX PLUS_DI MINUS_DI PLUS_DM MINUS_DM
AROON AROONOSC MOM ROC ROCP ROCR ROCR100 BOP IBS QSTICK WAD ASI SI IMI AO AC DPO ER FOSC CTI VHF WILLR
FRACTAL CCI CHOP CHOPTR VORTEX MFI ULTOSC CMO CMOU CG APO PPO TRIX COPPOCK ERI DOSC FISHER PSO SMI TSI
WAVETREND KST KSTEXT KDJ STOCHRSI CRSI STC SQZMOM. Files: `mom_wilder.zig`, `mom_simple.zig`, `mom_cg.zig`,
`mom_comp.zig`, `mom_comp2.zig`; plumbing `mom_util.zig` (scratch rings, `peek` for cores that own them) and
`vs_kit.zig` (identical to the copy of the volume / statistic wave).

API points beyond the seed: multi-input streams take a struct (`update(.{ .high, .low, .close })`), single-series
ones `update(x)`; multi-output functions take one slice per output in TA-Lib's order (`aroon`: down, up;
`vortex`: plus, minus; `kst`: kst, signal); parameterless functions (`bop`, `ibs`, `wad`) have
`<name>Lookback()`; functions that keep derived-series history in scratch (ADXR, AC, DOSC, WAVETREND, KST,
KSTEXT, STOCHRSI, CRSI, STC, SQZMOM) and the integer-output ones (FRACTAL, SQZMOM) take `gpa` first after `T`;
FRACTAL / SQZMOM write `[]i8` (100 / 0, resp. -1..3) with 0 in the lead. A single `unstable` option drives every
unstable id of one function (TA-Lib's process-global setting applies to all at once): the EMA / RSI stages
and, for FISHER and STC, their own id with its AUTO constants (FISHER 40 / 63, STC `(5*10+1)/2 + 3(slow+1)` /
`(5*19+1)/2 + 3(slow+1)`).

TA-Lib quirks found in the C (all kept, each pinned by the oracle):

- **ADX / ADXR / DX** use the two-stage `KEEP_IF_GT` selection and `dm -= dm/p; dm += dm1`; **±DI / ±DM** use
  `max(decayed, decayed + dm1)` (a negative dm1 is dropped) and a separate period-1 branch (DI = dm / TR without the
  factor 100). DX repeats its previous output when the true range is 0 or the DIs sum to ~0 (0.0 for the first
  one); the unstable AUTO constants differ per id (ADX 16p / 25p, DX 10p / 19p, DM `(10(2p-1)+1)/2`).
- **AO / AC / DPO / VORTEX / ULTOSC / KST / SQZMOM**: running sums start at the first window bar of the first
  output, not at bar 0 (the doubles differ in the last bits otherwise); a core is fed `largest lookback - own
  lookback` bars late, as for the seed composites.
- **CCI** sums its window in slot order of TA-Lib's circular buffer, not chronologically; **ER, MFI, ULTOSC,
  VORTEX, CMOU** zero their running sums after a window of exactly flat bars (`nullRun`) so no residue is left;
  **FOSC, CTI, CG** re-anchor their regression sums (32 periods, or on cancellation); **CG** keeps the window
  sums as 2 or 3 exactly-added integer limbs and re-derives the scale when a value no longer fits.
- **CRSI** composes `statistic.PercentrankCore`, **SQZMOM** `bands.VarCore` (the variance core STDDEV and VAR
  share), `overlap.MidpriceCore` and `statistic.LinearregCore`: the momentum wave's private copies are gone
  (the oracle agreement is unchanged).
- **APO / PPO** default to EMA (not SMA); PPO answers 0 when the slow MA is ~0 and, for windowed MA types, when the
  whole slow window is exactly zero. **KDJ** defaults to RMA (type 13, as in TA-Lib), and APO, PPO, KSTEXT, KDJ and
  STOCHRSI accept every `MaType` (the overlap wave's types and MAMA included).
- **PSO**: `tanh` is `xmath.tanh` (fdlibm's `expm1`-based form, as in glibc; Zig's `std.math.tanh` is musl's and
  differs by an ULP), the same function as the TANH transform. 16 of 20930 values differ from glibc by at most
  2 ULP (glibc's `expm1` against `std.math.expm1`): the ULP bound of PSO is 2, every other function is bitwise.
  (The momentum wave's private copy of the same formula had no NaN branch and gave 1 for NaN; it measured the
  same 16 / 2 on PSO and 31878 of 31883 bitwise on TANH against `xmath.tanh`'s 31880, so it was dropped.)
- ASI / SI refuse a limit move outside `[1e-8, 3e37]` (NaN included).

Anchoring: the live oracle covers all 57 (grid in `tools/interop.zig`: defaults, edges, swaps, every `MaType` where one is a parameter (APO, PPO, KSTEXT in both slots, KDJ, STOCHRSI: all bitwise, MAMA in the slot included), out-of-range values, unstable 0 / 3 / AUTO4 / AUTO8, lengths up to 5000,
f64 and f32), frozen replay in `src/oracle_test.zig`. Not covered: NaN input, other toolchains.
